name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__add_chart_to_dashboard
description:
Add a new chart to a dashboard. Use the `section` parameter to organize charts into named sections — sections are auto-created if they don't exist, and charts are auto-positioned within them.

**REQUIRED**: the `query`'s FROM must reference a source, either `{{source}}` or a source-type variable defined via `set_dashboard_variable` (e.g. `{{redis_source}}`). A query with no source is rejected with guidance to define it first.

Dashboard chart queries run against the metrics collection: use `sum(logs_count)` (or the matching `sum(<row_type>_count)` for the source), `avgMerge(value_avg)`, `label('tag')`. Do NOT use `JSONExtract(raw, ...)` — that is for live-tail charts and `query` only; dashboards have no `raw` column. Call `metrics_query_help` with the source ID **and `context: 'chart_query'`** for available metrics/labels and chart-query-style examples.

**Workflow:**
1. Call `chart_building_help` for chart types, units, and settings.
2. Call `metrics_query_help` with `context: 'chart_query'` to see the source's metrics schema and chart-query examples.
3. Verify the query with `render_chart` (runs it and surfaces errors automatically) or with `query`.

Use `{{source}}`, `{{start_time}}`, `{{end_time}}`, `{{time}}` variables for integration with dashboard filters. Queries can also reference custom dashboard variables — `{{var}}` (required) or `[[ AND col = {{var}} ]]` (optional clause, dropped while the variable is empty); define them with `set_dashboard_variable`.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__add_dashboard_section
description: Add a section divider to a dashboard. Sections span the full width and help organize charts into groups. Charts and sections at or below the insertion point are shifted down to make room

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__add_escalation_policy_step_member
description: Add a member to an escalation step of an escalation policy, for example an outgoing webhook (type webhook) so the step fires it, or a user, an on-call calendar or a Slack integration. With new_step, the member goes alone into a new escalation step at step_number instead, and the steps from there on move one later: a webhook in a new step 1 fires first, and next_step_wait_minutes gives it time before the people in the next step are notified. The policy keeps its other steps and members

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__application

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__applications

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__available_incident_escalation_policies

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__catalog_relation
description:
Show one catalog relation with its records, one column per attribute, paginated. Objects read as
`Platform (Team 123)`, so a record can name them again by `name` or `item_id`.
See `catalog_relations` for how the catalog works.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__catalog_relations
description:
List the catalog's relations with their primary and added attributes and how many records each holds.

## How the catalog works

The catalog adds business context to incidents through lookup tables.

- A **relation** is a table. Its **primary attributes** are the key columns, its **added attributes** are the columns it adds, and each **record** is a row.
- A primary attribute is named after a metadata key incidents already carry, set by a monitor, an integration, the reporter or another relation. When an incident's value for that key equals a record's primary value exactly, the record's added values are copied onto the incident as metadata, where escalation policies can act on them.
- With several primary attributes, the relation's matching decides: `any` matches a record when one of its primary values matches, `all` only when every primary attribute does, an empty primary cell matching anything there. A record with every primary cell empty is the relation's fallback, used only when no other record matches.
- A value is text, or a Better Stack object: `Team`, `User` (a team member), `Policy` (an escalation policy), `Schedule` (an on-call calendar), `Endpoint` (a monitor) and more. Reference an object by `name` (a team member by `email`) or by the `item_id` that `catalog_relation` shows, a monitor by `item_id` only; the team IDs other tools take are a different number.
- An added attribute named like another relation's primary attribute chains the lookup: the value it adds is looked up in that relation next.
- Three added attributes draw the Dependencies map on Integrations → Catalog:
  - `Dependencies`: the records this one needs, named by their primary value. An incident on any of them marks this record as affected too.
  - `Connections`: the records this one talks to, drawn without passing incidents on.
  - `Type`: Database, Storage, Frontend, Backend, Mobile app or Desktop app, which sets the record's icon.

Read one relation's records with `catalog_relation`.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__change_team_member_role
description:
Change a team member's role. Identify the member by `email` or `user_id`
(from team_members) and pass the target `role_id` (from team_roles). The
admin role cannot be assigned, and an existing admin's role cannot be changed,
via the API. Pending invitations can't have their role changed — cancel and
re-invite instead. With an OAuth token you must be on the team and your role
there must be at or above the member's current role, as on the team members
page. If the token can reach more than one team, pass `team_id` (or `team_name`).

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__chart_alert

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__chart_building_help
description: Get comprehensive instructions for building charts and dashboards, including chart types, units, axis settings, column mapping, legend placement, layout tips, and common mistakes. Call this before creating or editing charts

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__clusters

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_application
description: Create a new application in Better Stack. Returns the created application details including ID, ingestion token, ingesting host URL, retention settings, and platform-specific integration documentation links with next steps for configuration

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_catalog_relation
description:
Create a catalog relation with its primary and added attributes in one call. Add records with
`upsert_catalog_records` afterwards. See `catalog_relations` for how the catalog works.

Propose the relation to the user first (its name, matching, attributes and a few example records)
and create it once they agree. For a relation describing services, add `Dependencies`,
`Connections` and `Type` as added attributes, so the Dependencies map can draw its records.

## Rules

- Name primary attributes after metadata keys incidents really carry. Check recent incidents' metadata with `incidents` and `incident` first: a key no incident carries never matches.
- Reference teams, team members, escalation policies and other Better Stack objects as objects, like `{"type": "Team", "name": "Platform"}`, never as their names in text.
- Never invent records. Every row comes from a source the user pointed you to (code, Terraform, Kubernetes, a Backstage catalog, the service map) or from the user.
- Prefer `upsert_catalog_records` to removing records and adding them again: it keeps every record it doesn't name, while removing them all empties the relation.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_chart_alert
description: Create a new chart alert on an existing chart. The chart must support alerts (line_chart, bar_chart, or tail_chart with time variables; Number charts take no new alerts). Call chart_alert_help for configuration reference. Use chart or dashboard first to find the chart ID

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_cloud_connection
description: Create a secure cloud connection for direct ClickHouse query access to logs, spans, and metrics data. Returns connection credentials (host, port, username, password), sample queries for each data type, and cURL command examples. Connections expire after 1 hour by default

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_collector
description: Create a Better Stack Collector, the agent that collects logs, metrics and traces from a Docker host, a Docker Swarm or a Kubernetes cluster. Returns the collector details, the collector secret needed to install it, the ID of the source its data goes to, and the installation guide for its platform

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_dashboard
description: Create a new dashboard. Optionally use a template to start with pre-configured charts. Call chart_building_help for guidance on dashboard structure and layout. Optionally specify a source_id to preconfigure the dashboard with that source. Returns the new dashboard ID which can be used with add_chart_to_dashboard to add charts

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_error_comment
description: Post a comment on an error so the findings land in the conversation the team reads in Better Stack. The comment is written as the user whose token made the call and marked as posted via MCP, so a team member can tell it apart from one typed in the app; a call made with an API token is attributed to the API instead. When the error is linked to a Linear issue whose integration syncs comments, the comment is posted on that issue too. Use error_comments to read the conversation back.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_error_issue
description: Create an issue for an error in Linear, or a work item in Jira, through the team's integration and link the two. The issue gets Better Stack's standard body (error type, message, call site, stack trace, occurrence counts and a link back) and the integration's configured defaults for team or space, work type, assignee, labels and priority. Better Stack then posts every change to the error state as a comment on the issue. An error that already has an issue through the integration is reported, not duplicated; use link_error_issue to attach an issue that already exists.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_heartbeat
description:
Create a new heartbeat that expects a periodic request from a cron job, worker, or
other background task, and alerts when that request stops arriving.

Provide a `name` for the heartbeat. The heartbeat reports down once no request is
received within `period` seconds plus the `grace` window. Use the returned heartbeat
URL as the endpoint your job pings on every successful run.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_incident
description:
Create a new incident providing a summary of the issue, requester email, and other optional details.
Notification channels (call, sms, email, critical_alert) all default to false, so an incident with none of them set reaches nobody unless an escalation policy handles it.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_incident_comment
description: Create a comment on an incident

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_metric_expression
description:
Create a new metric expression (extract-metrics-from-logs rule) on a source.

`sql_expression` runs against each log row; log fields live inside the `raw` JSON column — use `JSONExtract(raw, 'path', 'Nullable(Type)')`. The `Nullable(...)` wrapper is required. Nested paths use positional args: `JSONExtract(raw, 'request', 'headers', 'user-agent', 'Nullable(String)')`. Call `source_fields` to see what fields exist.

Pass `aggregations` (e.g. `["avg", "count"]`) for an aggregated metric, or omit / pass `[]` for a label (group-by column).

Prefer `build_type: new_data` (default). `historical_logs` re-runs the rule over every stored log — expensive; only when the user explicitly asks.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_monitor
description:
Create a new monitor that tracks the availability of a website, host, or service.

Provide the `url` to monitor. For ping, TCP, UDP, SMTP, POP, IMAP, and DNS monitors
this is the host (e.g. `example.com`) rather than a full URL. The monitor starts
checking immediately unless `paused` is set to true.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_outgoing_webhook
description: Create an outgoing webhook: Better Stack sends a request to the URL when incidents change (or on-call, or monitors). An incident webhook fires for incidents without an escalation policy when notify_alongside_primary_responder is on (the default), and for incidents with one only once it is added to a step of that policy in Better Stack. Incident events you do not pass are on. Set a custom request with http_method, headers, body_template and basic authentication. Header values and credentials are stored but never shown back

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_release
description: Register a release for an errors application, so it appears the moment it deploys instead of when its first error arrives. Returns the release ID, usable with remove_release

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__create_source

Returns the created source details including ID, ingestion token, ingesting host URL, retention settings, and platform-specific integration documentation links with next steps for configuration. To set up a Better Stack Collector on Docker, Docker Swarm or Kubernetes, use create_collector instead

The query uses template variables (`{{source}}`, `{{time}}`, `{{start_time}}`, `{{end_time}}`) and runs against the source's metrics collection — it is meant to be saved as a dashboard chart via `add_chart_to_dashboard` / `edit_chart`, NOT run directly.

description: List all available data regions and clusters for application and source creation. Returns a table with region IDs (to use when creating applications or sources), display names, types (Region or Cluster), and geographical locations. Includes usage instructions for both standard regions and custom clusters

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__delete_catalog_records
description:
Remove catalog records by their primary values, or every record of a relation with `all: true`. A
record is removed when its primary values equal a given row's, as `upsert_catalog_records` matches
them; a row matching several records removes none of them. See `catalog_relations` for how the catalog works.

## Rules

- Name primary attributes after metadata keys incidents really carry. Check recent incidents' metadata with `incidents` and `incident` first: a key no incident carries never matches.
- Reference teams, team members, escalation policies and other Better Stack objects as objects, like `{"type": "Team", "name": "Platform"}`, never as their names in text.
- Never invent records. Every row comes from a source the user pointed you to (code, Terraform, Kubernetes, a Backstage catalog, the service map) or from the user.
- Prefer `upsert_catalog_records` to removing records and adding them again: it keeps every record it doesn't name, while removing them all empties the relation.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__delete_chart_alert
description: Delete a chart alert permanently. This will also clean up any associated incidents and anomaly models. This action cannot be undone. Use chart_alerts or chart_alert first to find the alert ID

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__delete_metric_expression
description:
Delete a metric expression from a source. This action cannot be undone. Call `metric_expressions` first to get the ID.

`build_type: new_data` (default) stops the rule from applying to future logs but leaves already-extracted data. `build_type: historical_logs` also rebuilds the source's metrics without this rule — expensive.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__documentation
description: Search for relevant documentation articles and return their contents

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__edit_application
description: Edit an existing application in Better Stack - rename it, pause or resume ingesting, or set its VRL transformations, including the exception grouping program. Only provide the fields you want to change. Use applications or application first to find the application ID.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__edit_chart
description:
Edit an existing chart name, query, type, or settings. Only provide the fields you want to change.

**If changing the query:** the new query's FROM must reference a source, either `{{source}}` or a source-type variable defined via `set_dashboard_variable` (queries with no source are rejected).

Dashboard chart queries run against the metrics collection: use `sum(logs_count)` (or the matching `sum(<row_type>_count)` for the source), `avgMerge(value_avg)`, `label('tag')`. `JSONExtract(raw, ...)` only works in live-tail charts — dashboards have no `raw` column.

Verify the new query with `render_chart` (runs it and surfaces errors automatically) or with `query` before saving.

Queries can also reference custom dashboard variables — `{{var}}` (required) or `[[ AND col = {{var}} ]]` (optional clause, dropped while the variable is empty); define them with `set_dashboard_variable`.

Call `chart_building_help` for chart/settings reference and `metrics_query_help` with `context: 'chart_query'` for the source's metrics schema and chart-query-style examples. Use `dashboard` first to find the chart ID.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__edit_chart_alert
description: Edit an existing chart alert configuration. Only provide the fields you want to change. Call chart_alert_help for configuration reference. Use chart_alerts or chart_alert first to find the alert ID

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__edit_dashboard
description: Edit an existing dashboard's name or source eligibility. Only provide the fields you want to change. Use dashboard first to find the dashboard ID.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__edit_dashboard_section
description: Edit an existing dashboard section. Only provide the fields you want to change. Use dashboard first to find the section ID

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__edit_slack_integration
description: Change the settings of a Slack integration, as on Integrations › Slack › Configure. Only the parameters you pass change. channel_invitees, alert_options and status_page_update_resources replace the whole list

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__error
description: Get comprehensive details of a specific error including its type, message, call site information, first occurrence, current state (unhandled, unresolved, ignored, resolved, or reoccurred), and linked Linear/Jira issues

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__error_comments
description: Read the conversation on an error: comments left in the app, comments posted by an agent over MCP, replies written in the error Slack thread, and comments synced in from a linked Linear issue. Every entry names its author and, when it did not come from the app, how it was posted; a comment left on one occurrence of the error names that event.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__errors
description: List error patterns for an application with occurrence counts, affected users, current state, and links. Defaults to unresolved errors and supports filtering by state. For specialized error analytics or custom SQL, use errors_query_help instead.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__errors_query_help

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__escalate_incident
description:
Escalate an ongoing incident to a user, team, on-call calendar, escalation policy, or the whole organization.
A policy brings its own notification channels; every other target needs at least one of call, sms, email, push or critical_alert.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__exploration

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__explore_logs_query_help
description:
Get instructions for writing a ClickHouse query to use inside the Better Stack **Explore logs** page (and live-tail charts) for log and span data.

The query uses template variables (`{{source}}`, `{{time}}`, `{{start_time}}`, `{{end_time}}`) and reads fields from the `raw` JSON column — it is meant to be used in the Explore UI, NOT run directly.

To instead write an ad-hoc logs/spans query you will run directly via `query`, use `query_help`.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__export_dashboard
description: Export a dashboard configuration as JSON. Returns the complete dashboard data structure including charts, sections, presets, and settings

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__heartbeat

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__heartbeat_availability
description: Get availability summary for a specific heartbeat

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__heartbeats
description: List all heartbeats with filtering and pagination options

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__import_dashboard
description: Import a dashboard from JSON configuration. Creates a new dashboard with the provided data structure. Pass exactly one of `data` or `url`. Writing a large JSON out in `data` is slow and can exceed your output limit, so when the JSON is over about 50 KB, put it at a URL Better Stack can download without credentials (for example a pre-signed S3 link) and pass `url` instead. Each chart's `settings` follow chart_building_help. A chart with `unit: "percent"` takes a 0-1 ratio and multiplies it by 100 (0.75 renders as 75%), so never multiply by 100 in its query; divide a 0-100 value by 100 instead. The threshold `value`s of its `chart_alerts` are 0-1 too (0.85 for 85%); a `relative` alert's `value` stays a percentage change (50 for 50%). A `stacking: "stack_to_100"` bar chart is the exception: its query and thresholds stay raw values

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__incident
description: Get detailed information about a specific incident

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__incident_timeline

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__invite_team_member
description:
Invite someone to a Better Stack team by e-mail address. Optionally set their
role by system-role name (`role`: responder, member, team_lead, billing_admin)
or by `role_id` (use team_roles to look up ids). Defaults to responder. The
admin role cannot be assigned via the API. Someone who already belongs to
the organization is added to the team directly, with no invitation to
accept; the Admin role applies to every team, so an existing Admin keeps it.
If the token can reach more than one team, pass `team_id` (or `team_name`).

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__link_error_issue
description: Link an error to an issue or work item that already exists in Linear or Jira. Better Stack then posts every change to the error state as a comment on the issue. For Linear, resolving the issue also resolves the error when auto-resolve is turned on for that integration; Jira has no status sync back. Create the issue in Linear or Jira first, then pass its identifier, key, or URL here.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__metric
description: Get comprehensive details about a specific metric. Returns metric overview (data points, active series, available aggregations), definition (SQL expression or JSON path), example queries for different aggregation functions, and Prometheus tags (for pure metrics). Essential for understanding how to query and use a metric

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__metric_expressions
description: List the metric expressions (extract-metrics-from-logs rules) on a source. Returns the rule ID, name, kind (metric vs label), ClickHouse type, SQL expression, and aggregations. IDs use a short prefixed form that feeds straight into update_metric_expression / delete_metric_expression

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__metrics_query_help
description:
Get instructions for building SQL ClickHouse queries for metrics (available metrics, aggregations, examples) to run directly via the query tools (`query` / `render_chart`), written as templates (`FROM {{source}}`, `{{start_time}}`, `{{end_time}}`, `{{time}}`) that the tools expand from their `source_type`, `start_time` and `end_time` arguments.

To instead write a query for use inside a Dashboard chart, use `dashboard_query_help`.

Pass `context: 'chart_query'` when the query will be saved as a dashboard chart or chart alert — the prompt will emphasize `{{source}}` / `{{time}}` / `{{start_time}}` / `{{end_time}}` template variables and chart column aliases. (`context: 'direct_query'` is the default, for ad-hoc queries.)

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__metrics_schema
description: Get metrics and cardinality for a source. Returns a paginated table of available metrics (user-defined and ingested) ordered by active series (highest cardinality first), with their names, types, storage layout, data points count, and active series count. Use `name_filter` to search by name: `rabbitmq*`, `*queue*`, `*_total`, or an exact name. When more than 250 metrics match and grouping them by name prefix would shrink the list at least 3x, a prefix summary is returned instead of the list; drill in with the `name_filter` it suggests. `page` applies to whichever table is shown

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__query
description:
Execute a ClickHouse SQL query to retrieve logs, traces/spans, errors, and metrics from telemetry data.

Write the query as a template and the server builds the collections for you, as Better Stack's dashboards and AI SRE do:
- `FROM {{source}}` reads the source's recent and historical rows of `source_type` together (for metrics, its metrics collection), scoped to the source
- `{{start_time}}` and `{{end_time}}` are the `start_time` and `end_time` arguments, e.g. `WHERE dt >= {{start_time}} AND dt < {{end_time}}`
- `{{time}}` buckets `dt` to an interval that suits the range (`toStartOfInterval(dt, INTERVAL '<n> second')`); `{{interval_seconds}}` is that interval
A template needs `source_type`, `start_time` and `end_time`, and no `table`. A query without `{{...}}` runs exactly as written, needs `table` and must name its `remote(...)` and `s3Cluster(...)` collections itself.

- **IMPORTANT**: Use `query_help` to get instructions on how to create the correct query for logs and spans
- **IMPORTANT**: Use `errors_query_help` to get instructions on how to create the correct query for errors
- **IMPORTANT**: Use `metrics_query_help` to get instructions on how to create the correct query for metrics
- Before a query over more than a few hours of logs, spans or other events, call `query_windows` with the same arguments: it says whether the range fits one call and, if not, the time windows that do. A template of either shape below needs no such call: `query` splits its range itself
- A template listing the newest rows (`ORDER BY dt DESC LIMIT n`, filtered by `dt >= {{start_time}} AND dt < {{end_time}}`, with no aggregate, `GROUP BY`, `DISTINCT` or subquery) whose range is too wide for one call is read one time window at a time, newest first, until it has its n rows; the result says how far it read and where to continue
- A template that only adds up or combines (`count()`, `countIf()`, `sum()`, `sumIf()`, `min()`, `max()`, beside the `GROUP BY` columns it selects; `ORDER BY` and `LIMIT` on those), filtered by `dt >= {{start_time}} AND dt < {{end_time}}`, with no `HAVING`, `DISTINCT` or subquery, whose range is too wide for one call but holds at most 300,000,000 rows is run in time windows, several at once, and the windows' rows merged; the result says how far it read

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__query_help
description: Get instructions for building SQL ClickHouse queries for logs and spans (fields, aggregations, examples) to run directly via the query tools (query / render_chart) against the ClickHouse proxy. To instead write a query for use inside the Explore logs UI, use explore_logs_query_help.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__query_windows
description:
Size an S3 query before running it: how many rows its time range holds and, when that is more than one `query` call reads (50,000,000 rows, 50 seconds), the time windows that fit one call each.

Pass the same arguments you would pass to `query` (`query`, `source_id`, and `table` for SQL without template variables or `source_type`, `start_time` and `end_time` for a template). Nothing is read from S3; the answer comes from the source's row counts in well under a second.

All timestamps are UTC; when `server_timezone` is not UTC, write each bound as toDateTime('<value>', 'UTC') rather than as a bare literal, which would be parsed in the server's timezone.

Every answer with a `decision` carries `notes`, what it says to do, written for this query: how to pass and merge its windows, what to replace before splitting a template that uses `{{time}}`, why the range could not be sized.

Returns `decision`:
- `run` — the range fits one call; run the query as written
- `windows` — Run the query once per window, newest first, with `dt >= '<from>' AND dt < '<to>'` in place of its time filter, and merge the results yourself: rows concatenate; `count()` and `sum()` add up; `min()` and `max()` combine; an average needs `sum()` and `count()` per window; `quantile(...)`, `uniq(...)`, `count(DISTINCT ...)` and `topK(...)` do not merge across windows, so keep those to one window or add filters. For a template whose time filter is `{{start_time}}`/`{{end_time}}`, pass each window as `start_time` = `from` and `end_time` = `to` instead. When `query` splits such a template itself (its description names the two shapes), `notes` says to call `query` once instead, and the windows are only a fallback. At most 200 windows are returned; `more_windows` counts the older ones the range still holds. More windows than you will run means the range needs rethinking: narrow the time filter, add filters on `raw` before extracting JSON, or set `sampling=` to `suggested_sampling` to estimate rather than measure. A window marked `oversized` holds more than the budget in a single second: add filters or `sampling=` for it
- `unsized` — the query's shape cannot be sized; `explanation` says what to change

With `run` or `windows`:
- `hot_tail` (never for a `{{source}}` template or a query that reads the hot collection itself with `remote()`) — the newest rows of the range are still in the hot collection, which `s3Cluster` holds only once they leave it: `from` is the oldest row still there (Live tail's first row on disk), `estimated_rows` how many of the range's rows that is, `collection` the hot collection to read them from when the row type names one; the top-level `estimated_rows` and the windows then count S3 rows only. Run the same query against `remote(<collection>)` with the time filter unchanged and no `_row_type` filter, and merge it in as one more window, without cutting the S3 windows at `from`: S3 already holds rows past it. Without `from` the boundary could not be probed and the range merely reaches into the last hours
- `hot_rows` (a `{{source}}` template, or a query that reads the hot collection itself, whose range is over the budget with its hot rows counted) — how many rows of the range are still in the hot collection: the query reads them too, but `estimated_rows` and the budget leave them out, since a hot read is usually fast. Without `hot_rows`, `estimated_rows` counts them. If the query still times out on them, the timeout lists windows that split them
- `suggested_sampling` — with more windows than you will run, the `sampling=` rate at which the whole range fits one call

Remove a member from a Better Stack team, or cancel a pending invitation.
Identify them by `email` or `user_id` (from team_members). Admins cannot be
removed via the API, and the organization's last member cannot be removed. If
the token can reach more than one team, pass `team_id` (or `team_name`). With
an OAuth token you must be on the team and your role there must be at or above
theirs, as on the team members page. This permanently removes the person's
access to the team.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__render_chart
description:
Execute a ClickHouse SQL query and visualize the result as a chart.

Use `chart_type` to choose the visualization:
- `line` (default) — trends over time. Alias columns as `time`, `value`, and optional `series`.
- `bar` — magnitude over time or across buckets. Uses the same columns as `line`; set `stacked: true` to stack the series.
- `pie` — share of a total across categories. Alias a categorical column `AS series` (the slice label) and a numeric column `AS value` (the slice size), e.g. `SELECT service AS series, count() AS value FROM ... GROUP BY service`.

Write the query as a template and the server builds the collections for you, as Better Stack's dashboards and AI SRE do:
- `FROM {{source}}` reads the source's recent and historical rows of `source_type` together (for metrics, its metrics collection), scoped to the source
- `{{start_time}}` and `{{end_time}}` are the `start_time` and `end_time` arguments, e.g. `WHERE dt >= {{start_time}} AND dt < {{end_time}}`
- `{{time}}` buckets `dt` to an interval that suits the range (`toStartOfInterval(dt, INTERVAL '<n> second')`); `{{interval_seconds}}` is that interval
A template needs `source_type`, `start_time` and `end_time`, and no `table`. A query without `{{...}}` runs exactly as written, needs `table` and must name its `remote(...)` and `s3Cluster(...)` collections itself.

Alias result columns as (line/bar):
- `... AS time` — the time bucket (e.g., `{{time}} AS time` in a template, or `toStartOfHour(dt) AS time`)
- `... AS value` — the numeric metric (e.g., `count() AS value`)
- `... AS series` — optional: a grouping column for multiple series (e.g., `service AS series`)

**IMPORTANT (line/bar): Always choose a time granularity that produces 50–500 data points** (`{{time}}` picks 30 seconds to 2 hours from the range, which is in that band up to a day but gives more points on longer ranges: bucket by hand there) — too few points make the chart useless, too many make it unreadable. Use these rules based on the query's time range:
- Up to 1 hour → `toStartOfMinute(dt) AS time` → ~60 points
- 1–24 hours → `toStartOfInterval(dt, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time` → up to 288 points
- 1–7 days → `toStartOfHour(dt) AS time` → up to 168 points
- 7–30 days → `toStartOfInterval(dt, INTERVAL 4 HOUR) AS time` → up to 180 points
- 30–90 days → `toStartOfInterval(dt, INTERVAL 12 HOUR) AS time` → up to 180 points
- 90+ days → `toStartOfDay(dt) AS time`

Additional query instructions (data access patterns) are in:
- `query_help` — logs and spans
- `errors_query_help` — errors
- `metrics_query_help` — metrics

Before a query over more than a few hours of logs, spans or other events, call `query_windows` with the same arguments: it says whether the range fits one call and, if not, the time windows that do.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__set_dashboard_variable
description:
Create or update a dashboard template variable — a user-facing filter in the dashboard toolbar, referenced in chart SQL as `{{name}}` (required — the chart errors until it resolves to a value) or `[[ AND col = {{name}} ]]` (optional — the whole `[[ ... ]]` clause is dropped while the variable is empty).

Saving a chart auto-creates a plain text variable (or a source variable when the name contains 'source') for any undefined required `{{name}}`, but it starts empty — use this tool to give it a typed definition or a default value so the chart resolves without manual input.

Fields per type:
- `select_value` (shown as "Static list") → the options in `default_values` (first = default selection)
- `select_with_sql` (shown as "Dynamic list") → an option-yielding **expression** (NOT a full query) in `sql_definition`, e.g. `label('_host')`; see the `sql_definition` parameter for how it is interpolated
- Both list types accept `allow_multiple_values: true` to let users pick several options at once (interpolates as a regex used with `match()`). `multi_select_with_sql` is the legacy always-multiple Dynamic list; prefer `select_with_sql` with `allow_multiple_values: true`.
- `select_predefined_sql` (shown as "Query per value") → named SQL filters in `filters` (each a **full query**), default picked via `selected_label`
- `string` / `number` / `boolean` → `[default]` in `default_values`
- `sql_expression` → `[raw SQL]` in `default_values`, spliced into chart SQL unescaped
- `source` → the source IDs in `source_ids`. Name it `source` to set the dashboard's own source (which sources every chart queries by default), or use a custom name for an extra source variable that a chart references in its FROM (e.g. `FROM {{name}}`) to query a different set of sources than the dashboard default.
- `date` / `datetime` → an ISO date in `default_values`, e.g. `['2026-07-23']` or `['2026-07-23T14:30:00Z']`

SQL-backed types are validated at save time by running their SQL against the dashboard's source — the save is refused when it fails.

The names `start_time`, `end_time`, and `time` are reserved (they come from the time picker). `source` is the exception: set it as a source-type variable to change the dashboard's source. Use `dashboard` to list a dashboard's variables and `dashboard_query_help` for how each type is referenced in chart SQL.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__set_exploration_variable
description:
Create or update a variable on an exploration (saved Explore query), referenced in its query as `{{name}}`.

The most common use is setting the exploration's source: name it `source`, type `source`, and pass the source IDs in `source_ids` — the query then runs against those sources.

Fields per type:
- `source` → the source IDs in `source_ids`. Name it `source` to set the exploration's own source, or use a custom name for an extra source variable the query references in its FROM (e.g. `FROM {{name}}`).
- `select_value` → the options in `default_values` (first = default selection)
- `select_with_sql` / `multi_select_with_sql` → an option-yielding expression (NOT a full query) in `sql_definition`, e.g. `label('_host')`
- `select_predefined_sql` → named SQL filters in `filters` (each a full query), default picked via `selected_label`
- `string` / `number` / `boolean` → `[default]` in `default_values`
- `sql_expression` → `[raw SQL]` in `default_values`, spliced into the query unescaped
- `date` / `datetime` → an ISO date in `default_values`, e.g. `['2026-07-23']` or `['2026-07-23T14:30:00Z']`

SQL-backed types are validated at save time by running their SQL against the exploration's source — the save is refused when it fails.

The names `start_time`, `end_time`, and `time` are reserved (they come from the time picker). `source` is the exception: set it as a source-type variable to change the exploration's source. Use `exploration` to list an exploration's variables.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__update_catalog_relation
description:
Change a catalog relation: rename it, change its description or matching, add attributes or remove
them. Only what you pass changes. Removing an attribute removes its values from every record.
See `catalog_relations` for how the catalog works.

## Rules

- Name primary attributes after metadata keys incidents really carry. Check recent incidents' metadata with `incidents` and `incident` first: a key no incident carries never matches.
- Reference teams, team members, escalation policies and other Better Stack objects as objects, like `{"type": "Team", "name": "Platform"}`, never as their names in text.
- Never invent records. Every row comes from a source the user pointed you to (code, Terraform, Kubernetes, a Backstage catalog, the service map) or from the user.
- Prefer `upsert_catalog_records` to removing records and adding them again: it keeps every record it doesn't name, while removing them all empties the relation.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__update_error_state
description: Update the state of a specific error (mark as resolved, ignored, or unresolved)

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__update_heartbeat

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__update_incident_comment

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__update_metric_expression
description:
Update an existing metric expression. Call `metric_expressions` first to get the ID.

At least one of `name`, `sql_expression`, `type`, `aggregations` must be provided — `build_type` alone is not a change and will be rejected. See `create_metric_expression` for `sql_expression` / `type` / `aggregations` guidance.

Prefer `build_type: new_data` (default). `historical_logs` re-runs the rule over every stored log — expensive; only when the user explicitly asks.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__update_monitor

Update a resource on a status page.

Change its public name, description, widget type (e.g. show or hide the uptime
history), or move it by setting `position` (zero-based) and/or
`status_page_section_id`. Use `status_page_resources` to find resource IDs.

name: mcp__claude_ai_betterstack__upsert_catalog_records
description:
Add or update a catalog relation's records, keyed by their primary values, so running the same sync
again updates instead of duplicating. A record whose primary values equal a row's is updated: the
added attributes the row names are replaced, the others are left alone. A row no record matches
becomes a new record. One invalid row fails the whole call and writes nothing. Up to 100
records per call. See `catalog_relations` for how the catalog works.

Name `Dependencies` and `Connections` by the other records' primary values.

## Rules

- Name primary attributes after metadata keys incidents really carry. Check recent incidents' metadata with `incidents` and `incident` first: a key no incident carries never matches.
- Reference teams, team members, escalation policies and other Better Stack objects as objects, like `{"type": "Team", "name": "Platform"}`, never as their names in text.
- Never invent records. Every row comes from a source the user pointed you to (code, Terraform, Kubernetes, a Backstage catalog, the service map) or from the user.
- Prefer `upsert_catalog_records` to removing records and adding them again: it keeps every record it doesn't name, while removing them all empties the relation.
